findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11(Q) Person In Charge. 11/13 inspection occurred as a result of confirmation of a falsified certified food manager certification present at the facility. Originally noted during the 11/12/26 inspection, inspector reached-out to SCDPH and ServSafe due to observation of the unique nature of the certificate. SCDPH observes 100s of certificates a year and this one presented with obvious doctored content. Upon confirmation, ServSafe did issue a certification to the individual in question, the certificate number and the expiration date are correct. The certificate given, however, is a false document that initially was issued to an employee Chase X. Someone doctored the available document. SCDPH recourse is to issue a follow-up to allow time for the facility to obtain proper certificates. 


The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (Q) Written procedures and plans, where specified by this Code and as developed by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, are maintained and implemented as required.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: During the 11/12 inspection, the certification presented appeared to be doctored. Upon investigation, the document presented was not for the correct person. McDonald’s has a fantastic in-house certification process and there are traditionally multiple CFPM present. Yesterday, the manager present did not indicate that anyone besides the single present party was certified. Be sure to educate managers that conversations with inspectors are key to good evaluations. If another certified person was present, this should have been indicated. Certified persons are present today.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed multiple TCS items to be held past their 7 day date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, items included biscuits and gravy, sweet tea, and Canadian bacon. Education was provided and items were discarded. Ensure any TCS item is discarded after 7 days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage.
